components.role: Most-changed MLP units, strongly active at the answer position; their output steers the queries of L10H1/L10H3/L11H1/L11H2/L11H3. Lowering them in A pulls L11 copy heads onto user-message content and moves L10H3 off the guess region, i.e. gates the routing to the user's guess.
Strongest copy head; in A its attention to the prompt-prefix sink (d about 27, base +183) drops by 66 logit units and it attends slightly more around d about 11.
Copy head; attends more in A to strongly attended keys about 9-10 tokens back (end of the user message, where the guess is stated).
Copy-suppression-like head; in A it attends less to keys about 11-12 tokens back (guess region) and more to the prefix, so the guess is suppressed less.
Global copy head; attends more to the end of the user message (d about 4) and less to the question and prefix in A.
Copy head in the global layer; keys steered by the L7 units; attends more to user-message content in A.
Previous-token-like head with the largest relative QK change in layers 0-10; its OV feeds the induction-style matching of L11H2/H3.
Final-layer copy head with the largest concentrated query change in layer 17; its changes sit at short distances (d 0-2), so its exact role is uncertain.
Copy-suppression-like global head; attends less to content in A.
Copy-suppression head; in A it attends less to the guess region and its token matching is weaker, so the guess is suppressed less.

evidence: Token-identity components (OV copying, induction matching, MLP self-amplification) are unchanged (about 0.1% relative), so the difference is attention routing. Sign-free logit ratios, sign-anchored logits (GeGLU constraints) and rotary-phase distance estimates show that A moves copy heads (L7H0, L10H2, L11H1, L12H2) from the prompt prefix (d about 24-30) to the end of the user message (d about 4-13; all heads z +2.0, prefix z -1.4) while copy-suppression heads (L10H3, L11H3, L15H1, L9H1) attend less there. The lowered L7 units 186/256 steer L11 queries away from content and L10H3 toward the guess region, so lowering them produces exactly this shift. Caveats: assumes the question precedes the guess; the prediction that B reads the question more was not confirmed; L17H1's dominant changes are local (d 0-2) and ambiguous.
